gloss: you (the one or ones spoken to)
summary: The pronouns of the one spoken to: אַתָּה “you” (a man), אַתְּ (a woman), אַתֶּם (men, or men and women together), אַתֵּן or אַתֵּנָה (women), and in scripture’s Aramaic אַנְתְּ and אַנְתּוּן. The verb already marks the person, so the pronoun is written where the one addressed is named or identified (“you are the man”, “you are dust”, “you are my son”), where he is set apart from others (“but you”, “as for you”), and beside a participle, which has no person of its own. Above all it is the word of prayer, “you are my God”, “you are he, the God, you alone”, and of God’s word to his son and his people, “you are my son; today I have begotten you”, “you are my witnesses”. No root with a meaning stands behind it: every Semitic language has the same pronoun, made of the pointing element ʾan- that “I” (אֲנִי) shares and the t that marks the second person in the verb; Hebrew has merged the n into the t, which Aramaic and Arabic keep.

words.summary: The masculine singular, 744 times (117 of them in the Psalms, where it is mostly said to God). Five times it is written without the final ה (את) and read אַתָּה (1Sa 24:19; Psa 6:4; Job 1:10; Ecc 7:22; Neh 9:6), and three times the short form אַתְּ is pointed for a man (Num 11:15; Deu 5:27; Ezk 28:14). It is not the object of a verb: for that Hebrew uses the suffix ־ךָ or אֹתְךָ. The database counts all the forms of “you” (1,092) under each of this entry’s Hebrew words, since the keys share their spellings; the figures given here are counted from the text.

senses.gloss: you (are): the one addressed named or identified
senses.definition: Stands as the subject of a clause with no verb, saying who or what the person addressed is: “you are the man”, “you are dust”; in a question, “are you …?”, “whose son are you?”.

evidence.note: אַתָּה הָאִישׁ: Nathan to David, “you are the man”.
כִּי עָפָר אַתָּה וְאֶל עָפָר תָּשׁוּב: “for dust you are, and to dust you shall return”.
מִי הִגִּיד לְךָ כִּי עֵירֹם אָתָּה: “who told you that you were naked?”, the first use of the word.
אַתָּה זֶה בְּנִי עֵשָׂו: “are you really my son Esau?” and he said, “I am” (אָנִי).
בֶּן מִי אַתָּה הַנָּעַר: “whose son are you, young man?”
הַאַתָּה צִיבָא: “are you Ziba?”, with the question particle.
הַאַתָּה זֶה עֹכֵר יִשְׂרָאֵל: Ahab to Elijah, “is it you, troubler of Israel?”
רְאוּבֵן בְּכֹרִי אַתָּה: “Reuben, you are my firstborn”.
כִּי עַם קְשֵׁה עֹרֶף אָתָּה: “for you are a stiff-necked people”: Israel addressed as one man.
מִן הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה שָׁם: “from the place where you are”.

senses.gloss: you (are): God naming his son, his priest, his servant
senses.definition: Yahweh’s own word to the one he appoints, saying what he is: “you are my son”, “you are a priest for ever”, “you are my servant”. The New Testament reads the first two of Jesus.

evidence.note: יַהְוֶה אָמַר אֵלַי בְּנִי אַתָּה אֲנִי הַיּוֹם יְלִדְתִּיךָ: “Yahweh said to me, you are my son; I have begotten you today”.
נִשְׁבַּע יַהְוֶה וְלֹא יִנָּחֵם אַתָּה כֹהֵן לְעוֹלָם: “Yahweh has sworn and will not repent: you are a priest for ever, after the manner of Melchizedek”.
וְאַתָּה יִשְׂרָאֵל עַבְדִּי: “but you, Israel, my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen”.
וְאָמַרְתִּי לְלֹא עַמִּי עַמִּי אַתָּה: “and I will say to Not-my-people, you are my people; and he shall say, my God”.
Paul at Antioch: God raised up Jesus, “as it is written in the second psalm, υἱός μου εἶ σύ” (Psa 2:7).
Both verses quoted together of Christ, who “did not glorify himself to become high priest”: υἱός μου εἶ σύ (Psa 2:7), σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα (Psa 110:4).

senses.gloss: you, as for you (the one addressed set apart)
senses.definition: Written beside a verb that already marks the person, it sets the one addressed apart: against someone else (“he … but you”), or turning to him with his own task or his own lot (“and you, lift up your staff”, “but you, go to the end”).

evidence.note: הוּא יְשׁוּפְךָ רֹאשׁ וְאַתָּה תְּשׁוּפֶנּוּ עָקֵב: “he shall bruise you on the head, and you shall bruise him on the heel”: “you” against “he”.
אַתָּה בָּא אֵלַי בְּחֶרֶב … וְאָנֹכִי בָא אֵלֶיךָ בְּשֵׁם יַהְוֶה: “you come to me with a sword … but I come to you in the name of Yahweh”.
וְאַתָּה הָרֵם אֶת מַטְּךָ: “and you, lift up your staff”, after what Yahweh himself will do.
וְאַתָּה אֶת בְּרִיתִי תִשְׁמֹר: “and you, you shall keep my covenant”, answering “as for me” (אֲנִי, 17:4).
וְאַתָּה לֵךְ לַקֵּץ וְתָנוּחַ וְתַעֲמֹד לְגֹרָלְךָ לְקֵץ הַיָּמִין: “but you, go to the end; and you shall rest, and stand in your lot at the end of the days”.
וְאַתָּה אַל תִּירָא עַבְדִּי יַעֲקֹב: “and you, do not fear, my servant Jacob”.
וְאַתָּה בֵּית לֶחֶם אֶפְרָתָה: “and you, Bethlehem Ephrathah … from you shall come out for me one to be ruler in Israel”: a town addressed; quoted in Mat 2:6.
הַאַתָּה תִּבְנֶה לִּי בַיִת: “is it you who will build me a house?”
צַדִּיק אַתָּה מִמֶּנִּי כִּי אַתָּה גְּמַלְתַּנִי הַטּוֹבָה וַאֲנִי גְּמַלְתִּיךָ הָרָעָה: Saul to David, “you have done me good, and I have done you evil”.
καὶ σὺ Βηθλεέμ, Peshitta ܐܦ ܐܢܬܝ ܒܝܬ ܠܚܡ: Mic 5:1 quoted.

senses.gloss: you (with a participle)
senses.definition: Beside a participle, which has no person of its own, it is the subject of what the one addressed is doing: “on which you are standing”, “what do you see?”.

evidence.note: הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה עוֹמֵד עָלָיו אַדְמַת קֹדֶשׁ הוּא: “the place on which you are standing is holy ground”.
מָה אַתָּה רֹאֶה יִרְמְיָהוּ: “what do you see, Jeremiah?”, answered אֲנִי רֹאֶה, “I see”.
כָּל הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה רֹאֶה לְךָ אֶתְּנֶנָּה: “all the land which you see, to you I will give it”.
הָאָרֶץ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה שֹׁכֵב עָלֶיהָ: “the land on which you are lying”.
בִּשְׁאוֹל אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה הֹלֵךְ שָׁמָּה: “in Sheol (the grave), where you are going”.

senses.gloss: you and … (joining others to the subject)
senses.definition: After a verb in the singular the pronoun is written out so that others can be joined to its subject: “you and your sons”.

evidence.note: וּבָאתָ אֶל הַתֵּבָה אַתָּה וּבָנֶיךָ וְאִשְׁתְּךָ: “and you shall come into the ark, you and your sons and your wife”.
לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה כָל מְלָאכָה אַתָּה וּבִנְךָ וּבִתֶּךָ: “you shall not do any work, you and your son and your daughter”.
בֹּא אַתָּה וְכָל בֵּיתְךָ אֶל הַתֵּבָה: “come, you and all your house, into the ark”.
לְמַעַן תִּחְיֶה אַתָּה וְזַרְעֶךָ: “that you may live, you and your seed”.
נִכְרְתָה בְרִית אֲנִי וָאָתָּה: “let us cut a covenant, I and you”.

senses.gloss: you too, even you (after a suffix or with גַּם)
senses.definition: After a suffix of the second person the free pronoun repeats it to stress it, “your blood, even yours”; with גַּם or אַף, “you also”.

evidence.note: יָלֹקּוּ הַכְּלָבִים אֶת דָּמְךָ גַּם אָתָּה: “the dogs shall lick your blood, even yours”.
הוֹדַעְתִּיךָ הַיּוֹם אַף אָתָּה: “I have made (them) known to you today, even to you”.
גַּם אַתָּה לֹא תָבֹא שָׁם: “you also shall not go in there”.
גַּם אַתָּה שְׁתֵה: “drink, you also”.

senses.gloss: you (God addressed in prayer and praise)
senses.definition: The word by which a man speaks to God: confessing who he is (“you are my God”, “you are our father”), what he alone has done (“you made the heavens”), and that he stays when all else passes. Most of the Psalms’ uses are of this kind.

evidence.note: וּמֵעוֹלָם עַד עוֹלָם אַתָּה אֵל: “from everlasting to everlasting you are God”.
וַאֲנִי עָלֶיךָ בָטַחְתִּי יַהְוֶה אָמַרְתִּי אֱלֹהַי אָתָּה: “but I have trusted in you, Yahweh; I said, you are my God”.
אַתָּה יַהְוֶה אָבִינוּ גֹּאֲלֵנוּ מֵעוֹלָם שְׁמֶךָ: “you, Yahweh, are our father; our redeemer from of old is your name”.
יַהְוֶה אָבִינוּ אָתָּה אֲנַחְנוּ הַחֹמֶר וְאַתָּה יֹצְרֵנוּ: “Yahweh, you are our father; we are the clay, and you our potter”.
מִבֶּטֶן אִמִּי אֵלִי אָתָּה: “from my mother’s womb you are my God”.
הוּא יִקְרָאֵנִי אָבִי אָתָּה אֵלִי וְצוּר יְשׁוּעָתִי: of David’s seed, “he shall call me, you are my father, my God and the rock of my salvation”.
לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי: “I will fear no evil, for you are with me”.
אִם אֶסַּק שָׁמַיִם שָׁם אָתָּה: “if I go up to heaven, you are there”.
אֲדֹנָי יַהְוֶה אַתָּה יָדָעְתָּ: “Lord Yahweh, you know”, to “can these bones live?”
הַיּוֹם יִוָּדַע כִּי אַתָּה אֱלֹהִים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וַאֲנִי עַבְדֶּךָ: “let it be known today that you are God in Israel, and I your servant”.
הֵמָּה יֹאבֵדוּ וְאַתָּה תַעֲמֹד … וְאַתָּה הוּא וּשְׁנוֹתֶיךָ לֹא יִתָּמּוּ: “they shall perish, but you shall stand … but you are he, and your years shall have no end”; quoted in Heb 1:11–12.
σὺ δὲ διαμένεις … σὺ δὲ ὁ αὐτὸς εἶ, Peshitta ܘܐܢܬ ܩܝܡ ܐܢܬ: Psa 102:27–28 quoted.

senses.gloss: you are he; you alone (אַתָּה הוּא, לְבַדֶּךָ)
senses.definition: “You (are) he”: the confession that the one prayed to is the God, and he alone, who made heaven and earth; it answers Yahweh’s own “I am he” (אֲנִי הוּא).

evidence.note: אַתָּה הוּא הָאֱלֹהִים לְבַדְּךָ לְכֹל מַמְלְכוֹת הָאָרֶץ אַתָּה עָשִׂיתָ אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֶת הָאָרֶץ: Hezekiah, “you are he, the God, you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; you made the heavens and the earth”.
אַתָּה הוּא יַהְוֶה לְבַדֶּךָ אַתָּה עָשִׂיתָ אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם: “you are he, Yahweh, you alone; you made the heavens … and you give life to them all”.
אֲדֹנָי יַהְוֶה אַתָּה הוּא הָאֱלֹהִים וּדְבָרֶיךָ יִהְיוּ אֱמֶת: “Lord Yahweh, you are he, the God, and your words are truth”.
כִּי גָדוֹל אַתָּה וְעֹשֵׂה נִפְלָאוֹת אַתָּה אֱלֹהִים לְבַדֶּךָ: “for you are great and do wonders; you are God, you alone”.
וְיֵדְעוּ כָּל מַמְלְכוֹת הָאָרֶץ כִּי אַתָּה יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהִים לְבַדֶּךָ: “that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you, Yahweh, are God, you alone”.
וְיֵדְעוּ כִּי אַתָּה שִׁמְךָ יַהְוֶה לְבַדֶּךָ עֶלְיוֹן עַל כָּל הָאָרֶץ: “that they may know that you, whose name is Yahweh, you alone are Most High over all the earth”.
הֲלֹא אַתָּה הוּא יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהֵינוּ: “are you not he, Yahweh our God?”, against the idols of the nations.
אַתָּה הוּא מַלְכִּי אֱלֹהִים: “you are he, my king, God”.

senses.gloss: blessed are you (בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יַהְוֶה)
senses.definition: The form of blessing said to God.

evidence.note: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אָבִינוּ מֵעוֹלָם וְעַד עוֹלָם: David before all the assembly.
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יַהְוֶה לַמְּדֵנִי חֻקֶּיךָ: “blessed are you, Yahweh; teach me your statutes”.
υἱός μου εἶ σύ, ἐγὼ σήμερον γεγέννηκά σε: Psa 2:7.
Psa 2:7, “as it is written in the second psalm”.
σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα: Psa 110:4; again in Heb 7:17, 21.
σὺ δὲ διαμένεις … σὺ δὲ ὁ αὐτὸς εἶ: Psa 102:27–28.
καὶ σὺ Βηθλεέμ: Mic 5:1.

evidence.locator: PSA 2:7 word 8; PSA 110:4 word 5; PSA 102:27 word 3; PSA 102:28 word 1; MIC 5:1 word 1
evidence.note: σύ for אַתָּה in the verses the New Testament quotes.
σύ for אַתָּה in prayer: σὺ εἶ ὁ θεὸς μόνος for אַתָּה הוּא הָאֱלֹהִים לְבַדְּךָ.
γῆ εἶ for עָפָר אַתָּה: the Greek puts its verb where the Hebrew has only the pronoun.

parallels.note: Set after אַתָּה as its predicate, “you are he”, as after אֲנִי in “I am he”.

evidence.note: וְאַתָּה הוּא.

opposites.note: The one spoken to against the speaker (also אָנֹכִי).

evidence.note: בְּנִי אַתָּה אֲנִי הַיּוֹם יְלִדְתִּיךָ.
אַתָּה … וְאָנֹכִי.
אַתָּה גְּמַלְתַּנִי הַטּוֹבָה וַאֲנִי גְּמַלְתִּיךָ הָרָעָה.
כִּי אַתָּה תִבְחַר וְלֹא אָנִי: “for you must choose, and not I”.

opposites.note: The one spoken to against the one spoken about (plural הֵמָּה).

evidence.note: הוּא יְשׁוּפְךָ רֹאשׁ וְאַתָּה תְּשׁוּפֶנּוּ עָקֵב.
הֵמָּה יֹאבֵדוּ וְאַתָּה תַעֲמֹד.
אֲנַחְנוּ הַחֹמֶר וְאַתָּה יֹצְרֵנוּ.

phrases.gloss: and you; but you, as for you

words.gloss: you (several; men, or men and women)
words.summary: The masculine plural, 283 times, most often in Jeremiah (40), Deuteronomy (29) and Genesis (26). It is the singular’s base with the plural ending ־ם of הֵם and of the suffixes ־כֶם, ־תֶּם. It serves for a mixed company, and Ezekiel has it beside the feminine in one verse, of the women who prophesy (Ezk 13:20) and of the flock that stands for men (Ezk 34:31).

senses.gloss: you (are): the ones addressed named or identified
senses.definition: Subject of a clause with no verb: what those addressed are.

evidence.note: מְרַגְּלִים אַתֶּם: Joseph to his brothers, “you are spies”.
בָּנִים אַתֶּם לַיהוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם: “you are sons to Yahweh your God”.
כִּי לִי הָאָרֶץ כִּי גֵרִים וְתוֹשָׁבִים אַתֶּם עִמָּדִי: “for the land is mine; for you are strangers and sojourners with me”.
כִּי אַתֶּם הַמְעַט מִכָּל הָעַמִּים: “for you are the fewest of all the peoples”.
עֵדִים אַתֶּם בָּכֶם כִּי אַתֶּם בְּחַרְתֶּם לָכֶם אֶת יַהְוֶה: “you are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen Yahweh”.

senses.gloss: you (are): what God calls his people
senses.definition: God’s own word to his people, saying what they are to him: his witnesses, his sons, “gods”, his flock; or, in judgment, “not my people”.

evidence.note: אַתֶּם עֵדַי נְאֻם יַהְוֶה וְעַבְדִּי אֲשֶׁר בָּחָרְתִּי: “you are my witnesses, says Yahweh, and my servant whom I have chosen”.
אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי אֱלֹהִים אַתֶּם וּבְנֵי עֶלְיוֹן כֻּלְּכֶם: “I said, you are gods, and sons of the Most High, all of you”, and then “but you shall die like man” (82:7); Jesus quotes it (Jhn 10:34).
כִּי אַתֶּם לֹא עַמִּי וְאָנֹכִי לֹא אֶהְיֶה לָכֶם: “for you are not my people, and I will not be yours”.

בִּמְקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יֵאָמֵר לָהֶם לֹא עַמִּי אַתֶּם יֵאָמֵר לָהֶם בְּנֵי אֵל חָי: “in the place where it was said to them, you are not my people, it shall be said to them, sons of the living God”; quoted in Rom 9:26.
וְאַתֶּם עֵדַי נְאֻם יַהְוֶה וַאֲנִי אֵל: “and you are my witnesses, says Yahweh, and I am God”.
וְאַתֵּן צֹאנִי צֹאן מַרְעִיתִי אָדָם אַתֶּם אֲנִי אֱלֹהֵיכֶם: “and you, my flock, the flock of my pasture, you are man; I am your God”.
ἐγὼ εἶπα, θεοί ἐστε, Peshitta ܕܐܠܗܐ ܐܢܬܘܢ: Psa 82:6 quoted.
οὐ λαός μου ὑμεῖς: Hos 2:1 quoted.

senses.gloss: you, as for you (those addressed set apart)
senses.definition: Beside a verb, setting those addressed against another or turning to them with their own part: “but you”, “you yourselves”.

evidence.note: וְאַתֶּם חֲשַׁבְתֶּם עָלַי רָעָה אֱלֹהִים חֲשָׁבָהּ לְטֹבָה: “and you, you meant evil against me; God meant it for good”.
יַהְוֶה יִלָּחֵם לָכֶם וְאַתֶּם תַּחֲרִישׁוּן: “Yahweh will fight for you, and you shall keep silent”.
אַתֶּם רְאִיתֶם אֲשֶׁר עָשִׂיתִי לְמִצְרָיִם: “you yourselves have seen what I did to Egypt”.
וְאַתֶּם תִּהְיוּ לִי מַמְלֶכֶת כֹּהֲנִים וְגוֹי קָדוֹשׁ: “and you shall be to me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation”; taken up in 1Pe 2:9.
וְהָיִיתִי לָכֶם לֵאלֹהִים וְאַתֶּם תִּהְיוּ לִי לְעָם: “and I will be your God, and you shall be my people”.
וְאַתֶּם פְּרוּ וּרְבוּ: “and you, be fruitful and multiply”.
כִּי אֲנִי יַהְוֶה לֹא שָׁנִיתִי וְאַתֶּם בְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב לֹא כְלִיתֶם: “for I, Yahweh, have not changed; and you, sons of Jacob, have not come to an end”.
הַאַתֶּם תְּרִיבוּן לַבַּעַל: “will you plead for Baal?”
ὑμεῖς δὲ γένος ἐκλεκτόν, βασίλειον ἱεράτευμα, ἔθνος ἅγιον, Peshitta ܐܢܬܘܢ ܕܝܢ: the words of Exo 19:6.

senses.gloss: you (with a participle)
senses.definition: The subject of a participle: what those addressed are doing.

evidence.note: אַתֶּם נִצָּבִים הַיּוֹם כֻּלְּכֶם לִפְנֵי יַהְוֶה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם: “you are standing today, all of you, before Yahweh your God”.
אֲשֶׁר אַתֶּם יֹשְׁבִים בְּאַרְצָם: “in whose land you are dwelling”.
וְאַתֶּם הַדְּבֵקִים בַּיהוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם חַיִּים כֻּלְּכֶם הַיּוֹם: “but you who held fast to Yahweh your God are alive, all of you, today”.

senses.gloss: you yourselves (after a suffix); you and …
senses.definition: After a suffix of the second person plural it repeats and stresses it; after a verb it lets others be joined to the subject.

evidence.note: הַעֵת לָכֶם אַתֶּם לָשֶׁבֶת בְּבָתֵּיכֶם סְפוּנִים: “is it a time for you, you yourselves, to dwell in your panelled houses?”
הִתְקַדְּשׁוּ אַתֶּם וַאֲחֵיכֶם: “sanctify yourselves, you and your brothers”.
οὐ λαός μου ὑμεῖς: Hos 2:1.
ὑμεῖς δὲ … βασίλειον ἱεράτευμα: Exo 19:6.

evidence.locator: HOS 2:1 word 19; EXO 19:6 word 1; HOS 1:9 word 7; GEN 50:20 word 1; EXO 14:14 word 4; ISA 43:12 word 8
evidence.note: ὑμεῖς for אַתֶּם.
θεοί ἐστε: Psa 82:6.

evidence.locator: PSA 82:6 word 4; DEU 14:1 word 2; EZK 34:31 word 6
evidence.note: θεοί ἐστε for אֱלֹהִים אַתֶּם; υἱοί ἐστε for בָּנִים אַתֶּם: the Greek verb stands where the Hebrew has only the pronoun.

opposites.note: The people against their God (also אָנֹכִי).

evidence.note: וְאַתֶּם עֵדַי … וַאֲנִי אֵל.
אַתֶּם לֹא עַמִּי וְאָנֹכִי לֹא אֶהְיֶה לָכֶם.
אֲנִי אָמַרְתִּי אֱלֹהִים אַתֶּם.

phrases.gloss: and you shall be my people

words.summary: The feminine singular, 57 times, said to a woman and to a city, land or people spoken of as one (Ezekiel 16 has it nine times of Jerusalem). Seven times the text writes the older, longer form אתי, with the final vowel that Arabic ʾanti, Ge'ez ʾanti and Akkadian atti keep, and it is read אַתְּ (Jdg 17:2; 1Ki 14:2; 2Ki 4:16, 23; 8:1; Jer 4:30; Ezk 36:13). The same short form is pointed three times for a man (Num 11:15; Deu 5:27; Ezk 28:14).

senses.gloss: you (are): the woman addressed named or identified
senses.definition: Subject of a clause with no verb: who or what the woman addressed is; in a question, “who are you?”, “whose daughter are you?”.

evidence.note: יָדַעְתִּי כִּי אִשָּׁה יְפַת מַרְאֶה אָתְּ: Abram to Sarai, “I know that you are a woman fair to look at”.
מִי אָתּ … אָנֹכִי רוּת אֲמָתֶךָ: “who are you?” “I am Ruth your handmaid … for you (אָתָּה) are a redeemer”: both genders in one verse.
בַּת מִי אַתְּ: “whose daughter are you?”
אִמְרִי נָא אֲחֹתִי אָתְּ: “say, please, that you are my sister”.
בַּאֲשֶׁר אַתְּ אִשְׁתּוֹ: Joseph to Potiphar’s wife, “because you are his wife”.
כִּי אֵשֶׁת חַיִל אָתְּ: “that you are a woman of worth”.
אֱמֹר לַחָכְמָה אֲחֹתִי אָתְּ: “say to wisdom, you are my sister”.
וְלֹא יֵדְעוּ כִּי אַתְּ אֵשֶׁת יָרָבְעָם: “that they may not know that you are the wife of Jeroboam”; written אתי.

senses.gloss: you (a city, land or people as a woman)
senses.definition: Said to Jerusalem, a land or a people addressed as a woman.

evidence.note: בַּת אִמֵּךְ אַתְּ … וַאֲחוֹת אֲחוֹתֵךְ אַתְּ: to Jerusalem, “you are your mother’s daughter … and you are the sister of your sisters”.
אַתְּ אֶרֶץ לֹא מְטֹהָרָה הִיא: “you are a land that is not cleansed”.
אַתְּ נָטַשְׁתְּ אֹתִי נְאֻם יַהְוֶה: “you have forsaken me, says Yahweh”.
גַּם אַתְּ תִּשְׁכְּרִי: to Nineveh, “you also shall be drunken”.
הֲלוֹא אַתְּ הִיא הַמַּחְצֶבֶת רַהַב: to the arm of Yahweh (a feminine noun), “are you not she who hewed Rahab?”
אֹכֶלֶת אָדָם אָתְּ: to the land, “you are a devourer of men”; written אתי.

senses.gloss: you, as for you (the woman addressed set apart)
senses.definition: Beside a verb or participle, setting the woman addressed apart, or naming the subject of what she is doing.

evidence.note: רַבּוֹת בָּנוֹת עָשׂוּ חָיִל וְאַתְּ עָלִית עַל כֻּלָּנָה: “many daughters have done worthily, but you have gone up above them all”.
וְאַתְּ הָיִיתְ בְּעֹכְרָי וְאָנֹכִי פָּצִיתִי פִי אֶל יַהְוֶה: Jephthah to his daughter, “and you are among those who trouble me; and I have opened my mouth to Yahweh”.
וְלָמָה אַתְּ שֹׁאֶלֶת אֶת אֲבִישַׁג: “and why are you asking for Abishag?”, with a participle.
כָּעֵת חַיָּה אַתְּ חֹבֶקֶת בֵּן: “about this time next year you shall embrace a son”; written אתי.
קוּמִי וּלְכִי אַתְּ וּבֵיתֵךְ: “arise and go, you and your house”; written אתי.
וְאַתְּ וּבֵית אָבִיךְ תֹּאבֵדוּ: “but you and your father’s house shall perish”.
וְאַתְּ שָׁדוּד מַה תַּעֲשִׂי: “and you, spoiled one, what will you do?”; written ואתי.

senses.gloss: blessed are you (בְּרוּכָה אַתְּ)
senses.definition: The blessing said to a woman.

evidence.note: בְּרוּכָה אַתְּ לַיהוָה בִּתִּי: “blessed are you of Yahweh, my daughter”.
וּבְרוּכָה אָתְּ אֲשֶׁר כְּלִתִנִי הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה מִבּוֹא בְדָמִים: David to Abigail.

senses.gloss: you (a man; the short form)
senses.definition: Three times the short form is pointed where a man, or God, is addressed.

evidence.note: קְרַב אַתָּה וּשֲׁמָע … וְאַתְּ תְּדַבֵּר אֵלֵינוּ: the people to Moses, “go near, you, and hear … and you shall speak to us”: אַתָּה and אַתְּ of the same man in one verse.
וְאִם כָּכָה אַתְּ עֹשֶׂה לִּי: Moses to Yahweh, “and if you deal thus with me”.
אַתְּ כְּרוּב מִמְשַׁח הַסּוֹכֵךְ: to the king of Tyre, “you were an anointed covering cherub”.

opposites.note: The woman spoken to against the speaker.

evidence.note: מִי אָתּ … אָנֹכִי רוּת.
וְאַתְּ … וְאָנֹכִי.

words.summary: The feminine plural, five times in all: אַתֵּן once (Ezk 34:31) and the longer אַתֵּנָה four times (Gen 31:6; Ezk 13:11, 20; 34:17). It is the base with the feminine plural ending ־ן of הֵן and the suffixes ־כֶן, ־תֶּן. Outside Genesis 31 it is said to things named by feminine nouns (the flock, hailstones) and to the women who prophesy in Ezekiel 13, where the masculine אַתֶּם stands beside it in the same verse. With five uses it rests on little, but the cognates have the same form.

senses.gloss: you (women, or feminine things, addressed)
senses.definition: The plural of אַתְּ: several women addressed, or a company named by a feminine noun.

evidence.note: וְאַתֵּנָה יְדַעְתֶּן כִּי בְּכָל כֹּחִי עָבַדְתִּי אֶת אֲבִיכֶן: Jacob to Rachel and Leah, “and you know that with all my strength I have served your father”.
וְאַתֵּנָה צֹאנִי: “and you, my flock, thus says the Lord Yahweh”.
וְאַתֵּן צֹאנִי צֹאן מַרְעִיתִי אָדָם אַתֶּם: “and you, my flock, the flock of my pasture, you are man”: feminine for the flock, masculine for the men it stands for.
אֲשֶׁר אַתֵּנָה מְצֹדְדוֹת שָׁם אֶת הַנְּפָשׁוֹת: to the women who prophesy, “with which you hunt the souls”; אַתֶּם follows in the same verse.
וְאַתֵּנָה אַבְנֵי אֶלְגָּבִישׁ תִּפֹּלְנָה: “and you, hailstones, shall fall”.
καὶ ὑμεῖς πρόβατα for וְאַתֵּנָה צֹאנִי.

words.summary: Scripture’s Aramaic “you”, fifteen times, always to a man: fourteen in Daniel, written אנתה throughout and read אַנְתְּ, and once in Ezra, written אנת (Ezr 7:25). It keeps the n that Hebrew אַתָּה has merged into its t, and the written form has the final vowel of Hebrew אַתָּה and Arabic ʾanta. The database links only nine of the fifteen to the word’s key.

senses.gloss: you (are): the man addressed identified
senses.definition: Subject of a clause with no verb, often with הוּא after it as Hebrew אַתָּה הוּא: “you are the head of gold”, “are you Daniel?”.

evidence.note: אַנְתְּה הוּא רֵאשָׁה דִּי דַהֲבָא: Daniel to Nebuchadnezzar, “you are the head of gold”.
אַנְתְּ הוּא דָנִיֵּאל דִּי מִן בְּנֵי גָלוּתָא דִּי יְהוּד: “are you Daniel, of the sons of the captivity of Judah?”
אַנְתְּה מַלְכָּא מֶלֶךְ מַלְכַיָּא: “you, O king, are king of kings, to whom the God of the heavens has given the kingdom”.
אַנְתְּ הוּא מַלְכָּא דִּי רְבַית וּתְקֵפְתְּ: the tree of the dream, “it is you, O king, who have grown and become strong”.

senses.gloss: you, as for you (set apart; with a participle)
senses.definition: Beside a verb or participle: turning to the one addressed, setting him against another, or naming the subject of what he does.

evidence.note: וְאַנְתְּ בְּרֵהּ בֵּלְשַׁאצַּר לָא הַשְׁפֵּלְתְּ לִבְבָךְ: “but you, his son Belshazzar, have not humbled your heart, though you knew all this”.
וְאַנְתְּ בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר פִּשְׁרֵא אֱמַר … וְאַנְתְּ כָּהֵל: “and you, Belteshazzar, tell the interpretation … but you are able”, against the wise men who are not.
אֱלָהָךְ דִּי אַנְתְּ פָּלַח לֵהּ בִּתְדִירָא הוּא יְשֵׁיזְבִנָּךְ: “your God, whom you serve continually, he will deliver you”.
אַנְתְּה מַלְכָּא חָזֵה הֲוַיְתָ: “you, O king, were looking, and behold, a great image”.
אַנְתְּ מַלְכָּא שָׂמְתָּ טְּעֵם: “you, O king, have made a decree”.
וְאַנְתְּ עֶזְרָא … מֶנִּי שָׁפְטִין וְדַיָּנִין: Artaxerxes’ letter, “and you, Ezra, appoint magistrates and judges”.
וְאַנְתְּ וְרַבְרְבָנָךְ … חַמְרָא שָׁתַיִן בְּהוֹן: “and you and your nobles … have drunk wine in them”: others joined to the subject.
σύ for אַנְתְּה: σὺ εἶ ἡ κεφαλή, “you are the head”.

words.summary: Scripture’s Aramaic plural, once, with the plural ending ־וּן where Hebrew has ־ם. One use fixes little by itself, but the Peshitta’s ܐܢܬܘܢ is the same word in constant use.

senses.gloss: you (with a participle)
senses.definition: The subject of a participle: what those addressed are doing.

evidence.note: מִן יַצִּיב יָדַע אֲנָה דִּי עִדָּנָא אַנְתּוּן זָבְנִין: the king to the Chaldeans, “I know for certain that you are buying time”.
ὑμεῖς for אַנְתּוּן.

words.gloss: you (one; ܐܢܬ, to a woman ܐܢܬܝ); you are
words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܐܢܬ (ʾat, the n written but not sounded), feminine ܐܢܬܝ, for σύ. After a word it also serves as “you are”, so that ܐܢܬ … ܐܢܬ, “you … you-are”, renders σὺ εἶ; and with ܗܘ, ܐܢܬ ܗܘ “you are he”, it is the form of the confessions made to Jesus and of God’s word to him.

senses.gloss: you (set apart; in prayer)
senses.definition: The one addressed, as Hebrew אַתָּה: set against the speaker, and said to God in prayer.

evidence.note: ܠܐ ܐܝܟ ܕܐܢܐ ܨܒܐ ܐܢܐ ܐܠܐ ܐܝܟ ܕܐܢܬ: Jesus to his Father, “not as I will, but as you”.
ܕܐܢܬ ܐܢܬ ܐܠܗܐ ܕܫܪܪܐ ܒܠܚܘܕܝܟ: “that they may know you, that you are the God of truth, you alone, and him whom you sent, Jesus the Messiah”.
ܘܐܢܬ ܩܝܡ ܐܢܬ … ܘܐܢܬ ܐܝܟ ܕܐܝܬܝܟ ܐܢܬ: “but you remain … but you are as you are”, Psa 102:27–28.
ܡܪܝܐ ܐܢܬ ܗܘ ܐܠܗܐ ܕܥܒܕܬ ܫܡܝܐ ܘܐܪܥܐ: the disciples’ prayer, “Lord, you are the God who made heaven and earth”.
ܐܦ ܐܢܬܝ ܒܝܬ ܠܚܡ ܕܝܗܘܕܐ: the feminine, “you also, Bethlehem of Judah”, Mic 5:1.

senses.gloss: you are; you are he (ܐܢܬ ܗܘ)
senses.definition: Saying who the one addressed is: “you are a prophet”, “you are my son”, “you are the Messiah”.

evidence.note: ܐܢܬ ܗܘ ܡܫܝܚܐ ܒܪܗ ܕܐܠܗܐ ܚܝܐ: Peter, “you are the Messiah, the son of the living God”.
ܐܢܬ ܗܘ ܒܪܝ ܚܒܝܒܐ: the voice from heaven, “you are my beloved son; in you I am well pleased”.
ܕܒܪܝ ܐܢܬ ܐܢܐ ܝܘܡܢܐ ܝܠܕܬܟ: Psa 2:7, “you are my son; I have begotten you today”.
ܕܐܢܬ ܗܘ ܟܘܡܪܐ ܠܥܠܡ: Psa 110:4, “you are a priest for ever”.
Nathanael: ܐܢܬ ܗܘ ܒܪܗ ܕܐܠܗܐ ܐܢܬ ܗܘ ܡܠܟܗ ܕܐܝܣܪܝܠ, “you are the son of God; you are the king of Israel”.
ܕܢܒܝܐ ܐܢܬ: the Samaritan woman, “(I see) that you are a prophet”: ܐܢܬ after the predicate as “you are”.
ܐܢܬ ܡܢ ܐܢܬ: “you, who are you?”
ܕܐܢܬ ܗܘ ܟܐܦܐ: “that you are Kepha (a rock)”.
ܡܒܪܟܬܐ ܐܢܬܝ ܒܢܫܐ: Elizabeth to Mary, “blessed are you among women”: the feminine as “you are”.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s plural ܐܢܬܘܢ (ʾattūn; feminine ܐܢܬܝܢ), for ὑμεῖς: the same word as Daniel’s אַנְתּוּן. Like the singular it serves after a word as “you are”.

senses.gloss: you (are): what the disciples are
senses.definition: Those addressed, named for what they are: “you are the salt of the earth”, “you are my friends”, “you are the temple of God”.

evidence.note: ܐܢܬܘܢ ܐܢܘܢ ܡܠܚܗ ܕܐܪܥܐ … ܐܢܬܘܢ ܐܢܘܢ ܢܘܗܪܗ ܕܥܠܡܐ: “you are the salt of the earth … you are the light of the world”.
ܐܢܬܘܢ ܪܚܡܝ ܐܢܬܘܢ ܐܢ ܬܥܒܕܘܢ ܟܠ ܕܡܦܩܕ ܐܢܐ ܠܟܘܢ: “you are my friends, if you do all that I command you”.
ܕܐܠܗܐ ܐܢܬܘܢ: “you are gods”, Psa 82:6.

cognates.note: Arabic keeps the n that Hebrew אַתָּה has merged into its doubled t, and the final -a that Hebrew writes with ה. Arabic grammar takes the word apart as أَنْ, the pronoun, and ت, “the sign of the person addressed”: the same ʾan that “I” (أَنَا, Hebrew אֲנִי) is made of, and the same t that marks the second person in the verb (Hebrew קָטַלְתָּ, תִּקְטֹל). That is the nearest thing to a root behind the word, and neither part has a meaning beyond pointing to a person.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 103, art. ان, أَنٌ
evidence.note: “It is also a pronoun denoting the person addressed, or spoken to, by assuming the form ↓ أَنْتَ [Thou, masc.]; ت being added to it as the sign of the person addressed, and أَنْ being the pronoun, accord. to the general opinion; the two becoming as one”.

“Added at the end of a noun, it is a particle of allocution: it is thus added in أَنْتَ [Thou], addressed to a male, and أَنْتِ [Thou], addressed to a female … It is added in [the beginning of] the second person of the future … as in أَنْتَ تَفْعَلُ [Thou dost, or wilt do]”.

doctrine.statement: Those who pray in scripture say “you” to one, and say that he alone is God: Hezekiah, “Yahweh, God of Israel … you are he, the God, you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; you made the heavens and the earth” (2Ki 19:15), “that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you, Yahweh, are God, you alone” (2Ki 19:19); the Levites, “you are he, Yahweh, you alone; you made the heavens” (Neh 9:6); David, “you are God, you alone” (Psa 86:10). Jesus prays in the same way. He lifts his eyes to heaven and says “Father” (Jhn 17:1), and then “this is life eternal, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you sent” (Jhn 17:3); in the garden, “not as I will, but as you” (Mat 26:39). From the verses: the “you” who alone is God is one person, the Father; Jesus speaks to him as another than himself, names himself beside him as the one he sent, and sets his own will under his.

Yahweh says to his anointed, “you are my son; I have begotten you today” (Psa 2:7), and swears to him, “you are a priest for ever, after the manner of Melchizedek” (Psa 110:4). The New Testament reads both of Jesus: the voice from heaven at his baptism, “you are my beloved son” (Mrk 1:11); Paul, that God fulfilled the promise “in that he raised up Jesus, as it is written in the second psalm, you are my son; I have begotten you today” (Act 13:33); Hebrews, that “Christ did not glorify himself to become high priest, but he who said to him, you are my son … as he says also in another place, you are a priest for ever” (Heb 5:5–6), and that God said this to none of the angels (Heb 1:5). Peter’s confession uses the same word back: “you are the Christ, the son of the living God”, which Jesus says his Father revealed (Mat 16:16–17). When he is charged with making himself God, Jesus answers from “I said, you are gods” (Psa 82:6) that scripture called those to whom the word of God came gods, and that what he said of himself was “I am the son of God” (Jhn 10:34–36). From the verses: God speaks to Jesus as “you”, one distinct from the “I” who begets him and appoints him; the son is begotten on a day and receives his priesthood from another; and his own claim is to be God’s son.

What God says the man is, he says with this word: “for dust you are, and to dust you shall return” (Gen 3:19). The sentence is on the man himself, the “you” who was taken from the ground, not on a part of him. The Preacher says where that “you” goes and what is there: “there is no work, nor reckoning, nor knowledge, nor wisdom in Sheol (the grave), where you are going” (Ecc 9:10). Even those God calls “gods, and sons of the Most High” are told “but you shall die like man” (Psa 82:6–7). From the verses: the man is dust and returns to dust; in the grave he neither works nor knows, and no rank exempts him.

The angel’s last word to Daniel is “but you, go to the end; and you shall rest, and stand in your lot at the end of the days” (Dan 12:13). A few verses earlier he has said what that standing is: “many of those who sleep in the dust of the ground shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to reproach, to everlasting contempt” (Dan 12:2). From the verses: Daniel himself is to rest, that is, to sleep in the dust, and then to stand at the end of the days; his hope is not a life continuing through death but waking from it, on the earth, at an appointed time.

What Israel is to God is said to them as “you”, and it hangs on hearing him: “if you will indeed listen to my voice and keep my covenant, you shall be my own possession … and you shall be to me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation” (Exo 19:5–6); “you are my witnesses, says Yahweh” (Isa 43:10). When they turn away the same word takes the name from them, “for you are not my people” (Hos 1:9), and promises it again: “in the place where it was said to them, you are not my people, it shall be said to them, sons of the living God” (Hos 2:1). Paul reads that promise of those God has called “not from the Jews only but also from the nations” (Rom 9:24–26), and Peter writes to such people in the words of Sinai, “but you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation”, who “once were not a people, but now are the people of God” (1Pe 2:9–10). From the verses: to be God’s people is his gift by his word, kept by hearing it, and it is given on the same terms to those of the nations whom he calls.

note: Drafted 2026-11-15. Root: keyed אנת, which is both the key the words are filed under and the root the text’s tokens carry (word_info root אנת for every Hebrew form), and no other entry has it. It is not a root with a meaning: the cognates show the pronoun itself in every Semitic language (Arabic ʾanta/ʾanti/ʾantum/ʾantunna, Akkadian atta/atti/attunu/attina, Ugaritic ʾat/ʾatm, Phoenician ʾt/ʾtm, Ge'ez ʾanta/ʾanti, Aramaic and Syriac ʾant/ʾantūn), and Arabic grammar (Lane pp. 103, 291) takes it apart as the deictic ʾan of “I” plus the t of the second person. The first-person entry ani.json (root אני) left אַתָּה out for this entry; the two share only that pointing element. The Hebrew words are given no `root` of their own, so the entry’s root joins them; the Aramaic words take the database’s keys אנתה and אנתונ; the Syriac words need none, SEDRA’s root being אנת. Counts: the five keys a.er.ab–af are matched by spelling to the same 1,092 tokens, so `lexicon-support` shows 1,092 for each Hebrew word; the true figures, counted from the text’s surfaces, are אַתָּה 744, אַתְּ 60 (57 to a woman, 3 to a man), אַתֶּם 283, אַתֵּן/אַתֵּנָה 5. BDB keys left unnamed: a.er.ac (אתי, the written form of אַתְּ, the same tokens as a.er.ad); a.er.aa (the root heading) and the cross-references a.gn.af, a.go.ae, a.gp.ac (no tokens). Aramaic: xa.bb.aa is linked only to the surfaces וְאַנְתְּ and אַנְתְּה (9 tokens); the six bare אַנְתְּ of Daniel (3:10; 4:19; 5:13, 18; 6:17, 21) carry no key, and those with ו (Dan 4:15; 5:22, 23) have the mistaken word_info root אונ. The text gives the qere at 1Sa 24:19; Psa 6:4; Job 1:10; Ecc 7:22; Neh 9:6 (ketiv את) and at the seven places written אתי. Not followed or not verified: Ge'ez plurals (ʾantəmu, ʾantən) are in Wiktionary’s Proto-Semitic descendant lists only, not as entries in the vendored file, so left out; Dillmann/Leslau, Segert, Krahmalkov, CAD A/2 atta not consulted, so Ugaritic, Phoenician and Ge'ez rest on Wiktionary alone; Old Aramaic ʾt (Sefire) in DEAPS not looked up; the Septuagint alignment has no rows for the feminine אַתְּ or for אַתֵּנָה in Gen 31:6, so no Greek is given for אַתְּ. A Peshitta verse for the feminine plural ܐܢܬܝܢ was not looked for. Heb 1:10–12 quotes Psa 102:26–28 (Hebrew numbering); it is cited under the sense and the Greek only, and whom Hebrews has in view there is left for the reviewer. Psalm verses are in the Hebrew numbering. No name entries: no personal name is formed from the pronoun (אִתַּי Ittai is from אֵת “with”).
